beats.text: You catch yourself looking at her body. Your eyes got there in a fifth of a second!
In an eye-tracking study, men's first look at a woman's photo landed on her chest or waist. Faster than two hundred milliseconds. Before her face.
But it's not just men. Here's the twist.
Women did it too! Asked to rate a woman's looks, both men and women looked longer at her chest and waist than at her face.
And being looked at has a cost. In an experiment, women whose bodies were stared at solved fewer math problems afterward. Men didn't.
So the first glance is fast. The stare is a choice. Look at her face.

ask: SEND THIS TO SOMEONE WHO STARES.
sources: Dixson, Grimshaw, Linklater & Dixson (2011), Eye-tracking of men's preferences for waist-to-hip ratio and breast size of women, Archives of Sexual Behavior 40(1), 43–50 – first fixations within 200 ms went to the breasts or waist; breasts looked at most often and longest; 0.7 waist-to-hip ratio rated most attractive.

Gervais, Holland & Dodd (2013), My eyes are up here: The nature of the objectifying gaze toward women, Sex Roles 69 – 29 women and 36 men; when evaluating appearance, participants (both sexes) focused more on women's chests and waists and less on faces; stronger for hourglass figures.

Gervais, Vescio & Allen (2011), When what you see is what you get: The consequences of the objectifying gaze for women and men, Psychology of Women Quarterly 35(1) – 67 women, 83 men; after an interviewer's body-focused gaze, women solved fewer of 12 math problems (about 6 vs just under 5); men's scores were unaffected.
